## Spot a perfect square {#perfect-square}

Look for two identical brackets or one bracket squared. Use $(a+b)^2=a^2+2ab+b^2$.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$(2x+5)^2$

::: {.fragment}

[Identify the two terms.]{.annotation}

$a=2x$, $b=5$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Substitute into the identity.]{.annotation}

$(2x+5)^2=(2x)^2+2(2x)(5)+5^2$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[The two FOIL cross products give $10x+10x$.]{.annotation}

$=4x^2+20x+25$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$(2x-5)^2$

Use the same identity. What value of $b$ gives the minus sign? Expand on paper.

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

$a=2x$, $b=-5$

$=(2x)^2+2(2x)(-5)+(-5)^2$

$=4x^2-20x+25$

Squaring $-5$ gives $+25$.

:::
